main_text.p: ad inania distractionem a te prætermittan- tur. ]

Fili, serva mandata mea, & vives, [non idealibus vanitatibus titillatus, sed vita vera & solide beata inde ditatus : ] & legem meam quasi pupillam oculi tui: [ inde enim animæ visus lumenque pendet. ]
Alliga eam digitis tuis, [praxi & exercitiis] scribe illam in tabulis cordis, [ in facultatibus constantis & ardentis desiderii & amoris. ]

Dic Sapientiæ, [Eruditioni veræ] Soror mea es: [macte animo, & oratione continua familiaritatem Sapientiæ Dei, Patris communis, quære, pete, spera ] & prudentiam [quæ omnia justo pretio æstimat & tractat] voca amicam tuam [ tuos affectus ei conservando. ]

Ut custodeat te a muliere extranea [ab Eruditione falsa, externas res solum & transeuntes respiciente ] & ab aliena ] quæ nec a Deo est, & vero cor ab eo alienat ] quæ verba sua facit dulcia [ verba eloquenter fucans, & splendidis promissis auriculas demulcens. ]
De fenestra enim domus mea per cancellos prospexi: [ab intimis ad externa meditationem meam traduxi. ]

Et vidi o parvulos [ video adolescentes inexpertos & ad quemvis ductum paratos :] considero vecordem juvenem [cui animus non est resistere vanitati, neque desiderare Creatorem suum in diebus juventutis suæ. ]

page.notes: Page number read as 360. The running head is set in small capitals. Several words in the first lines are faint and may be misread, notably "ad inania" and "Eruditioni". The bracketed glosses are printed inline in the text block, not in the margins, so they are kept in the paragraphs. The final line "ditioni" stands alone at the right of the last line and is treated as the continuation of the broken word "Eru-ditioni" rather than as a catchword.
